# Appeal of Denial — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-19**
**Member:** Riley Jennings
**Member ID:** W995720068
**Reference number:** POC-39DE00339B-16726
**Governing policy cited by plan:** UPMC Provider Manual Chapter G — Utilization Management (https://www.upmchealthplan.com/docs/providers/2025_ProviderManual_G.pdf), effective 2025-04-03

Dear UPMC Health Plan Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of my knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery (CPT 29881), which was denied on 2026-08-19 for "incomplete documentation" that did not allow a determination of medical necessity. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to review the complete record described below.

**A note on the policy language provided to me:** The excerpt I was given from UPMC Provider Manual Chapter G — Utilization Management concerns documentation requirements for prenatal and postpartum visits. That language does not appear to apply to a knee arthroscopy determination, and I have not been given the actual clinical criteria the plan used to evaluate my knee surgery request. Because I cannot verify what specific criteria were applied, I am unable to show point-by-point how my records meet them — and I do not believe the plan can have fairly evaluated my claim against the wrong criteria either. I am asking that this be corrected as part of the appeal review.

**Summary of the record that was submitted for review:**

- I have had 9 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- I completed 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-05-08 to 2026-07-17), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- I used NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-13 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- An MRI of my knee on 2026-07-18 showed a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, with preserved articular cartilage.
- I experience locking and giving way in my knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking.
- On exam, I have positive provocative testing on the affected side and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, and I do not smoke.

This is a substantial clinical record, including imaging, a documented trial of conservative treatment, and a specific functional impairment. If the plan's actual medical necessity criteria for arthroscopic meniscus repair require particular elements that it believes are missing, I am asking the plan to identify exactly what is missing so that my surgeon's office and I can supply it.

**Request for the criteria applied to my case.** I understand that UPMC Health Plan uses InterQual criteria, which is licensed software rather than a publicly posted document. Under ERISA and ACA appeal regulations, I have the right to receive, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on in denying my claim. I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination for CPT 29881, so that I can address the plan's actual concerns directly.

**Deadline and submission.** I understand my appeal must be received by 2027-02-15 (180 days from the date of the denial notice), though I am relying on the appeal address and process printed on my denial letter as authoritative. I am also submitting this appeal through the member secure website and by phone (1-888-876-2756 for group plans, 1-866-353-3598 for individual plans, TTY 711) to ensure it is received.

I ask that the plan reconsider this denial in light of the full clinical record, provide the specific criteria used to evaluate my request, and let me know promptly if any additional documentation is needed.

Thank you for your time and attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Riley Jennings
Member ID: W995720068
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date of signature]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
